1.explanation:
1. Copy the snippet above into a file named, for example, `blank-echo-test.qmd`.
2. Make sure you have Quarto v1.0.32 (or later) installed.
3. From the command line run:

   quarto render blank-echo-test.qmd --to html

4. Open the generated HTML in your browser. Under each chunk you will see the diagram (or graph) followed by the echoed source; notice that each echoed block begins with an unwanted blank line. This isolates the behavior seen in the bug report.
1.bug_scenario: When you include a mermaid or dot chunk in a Quarto document with echo enabled (either echo: true or echo: fenced), the rendered HTML shows an extra blank line at the very top of the echoed code block. In other words, the first non-empty line of the chunk (e.g. “flowchart LR” or “digraph { … }”) is always preceded by an empty line in the code mirror output.
